Gboard AI Writing Tools Flags: Rewrite, Style and Model Gates

Explore Gboard's writing tools controls and distinguish a visible rewrite button from actual on-device or service-backed generation.

What you should know

Writing Tools may involve multiple eligibility checks and model dependencies beyond a single enabled flag.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What the controls seem to separate

The Atlas includes enable_writing_tools_v2, enable_writing_tools_v2_on_toolbar, enable_writing_tools_suggest_style and enable_writing_tools_my_style. These names point at a product surface, its placement and style selection; they do not prove that a particular generative model is loaded. UI presentation and text generation are distinct functions.

Model gates are another layer

enable_ai_core_llm and other language-model identifiers suggest integrations with on-device or system AI components. But the exact requirements depend on Gboard and Android versions, language, device capability, downloadable assets and remote feature eligibility. Showing a button may be easier than producing a result, and an empty result is not necessarily a bug in the toolbar flag.

Test outputs responsibly

Use disposable text, not confidential messages. Compare neutral and formal rewrites, inspect whether the result preserves meaning and verify the destination text field before inserting it. Record whether an action is unavailable, fails to load or produces a response: those outcomes reveal different layers of a feature.

Frequently asked questions

Can one flag unlock all AI writing tools?

No single flag has been shown to bypass every language, model, device and rollout dependency.

Is a rewritten suggestion guaranteed private?

No. The flag name does not establish the processing location or data-handling policy.

Gboard Autocorrect Flags: Thresholds, Reverts and Corrections

Understand Gboard autocorrection experiments, confidence thresholds and why a correction can appear aggressive or hesitant.

What you should know

Autocorrection is a decision about whether to replace text; key correction and next-word prediction are related but different mechanisms.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What the AC threshold represents

In Gboard's research vocabulary, AC denotes auto correction. An identifier like enable_ac_threshold suggests a threshold-based correction decision. It does not reveal a public numeric threshold or guarantee that turning it on increases accuracy. Consider confidence thresholds as one ingredient in a decoder and suggestion pipeline, not an independent 'accuracy boost'.

Distinguish replacement from prediction

Autocorrection changes or proposes a replacement for text already typed, while next-word prediction offers what might come after it. Related flags can control revert behavior, bias from earlier corrections and UI presentation. These paths may interact, making before-and-after testing harder than judging one screenshot.

Get useful evidence

Test an intentionally misspelled phrase, a proper noun and a normal sentence on the same language layout. Record whether the inserted text is replaced automatically, which correction is suggested, and whether accepting or undoing one correction affects subsequent predictions. If you want less aggressive correction, prefer the normal Text correction settings first.

Frequently asked questions

Is enable_ac_threshold safe to force?

Its meaning is interpreted, not fully runtime-verified; forcing it can alter suggestions or have no visible effect.

Are AC and KC synonyms?

No. AC refers to auto correction and KC to key correction in Google-authored research terminology.

Gboard Clipboard History, Editing Tools and Patch Flags

Learn how clipboard retention experiments, editing shortcuts and Gboard Patches features differ from stock keyboard behavior.

What you should know

Clipboard content is potentially sensitive. Differentiate stock Gboard options from extra features added by Gboard Patches.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What stock and patched builds offer

Stock Gboard provides clipboard and text editing tools, while Gboard Patches documents enhancements to retention time, item count, preview formatting, backup/restore and a local-network web clipboard. These patched features are not proof that the same UI exists in every Gboard release. A flag that begins with pref_ may be a stored preference exposed by a patch.

The flags tell different stories

enable_extended_clipboard_history describes expanded historical behavior; pref_clipboard_ttl_ms refers to a retention period, not a Boolean. pref_force_cursor_trackpad_mode concerns editing navigation rather than clipboard storage. Data persistence, UI presentation and cursor movement should be tested independently.

Privacy before convenience

Clipboard histories may contain verification codes, private messages or financial text. Shorter retention can reduce exposure, while a web clipboard introduces LAN pairing and access considerations. The patch project documents controls, but the safest behavior depends on your configuration; don't expose a web clipboard without understanding how it authenticates and which network it can reach.

Frequently asked questions

Is pref_clipboard_ttl_ms an on/off switch?

Its name suggests a millisecond value; always inspect actual type before editing.

Is web clipboard built into every Gboard?

No. The cited Gboard Patches project adds its own web clipboard feature.

Gboard Developer Flags Explained: What Is Actually Hidden?

Understand Gboard's internal experiment flags, which identifiers are real switches, and why turning one on often changes nothing.

What you should know

A string recovered from an APK is evidence that an identifier exists, not proof that you can toggle a working feature.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

What counts as a flag

Gboard contains experiment gates, stored preferences, numeric thresholds, model selectors, diagnostics and version-specific settings. The Atlas catalogs identifiers found in a GboardWu 18.5.4 snapshot; it does not claim every string is a user-editable boolean. An apparently descriptive name can still point to a dormant experiment, an internal counter, or a parameter whose useful values are undocumented.

Read the identifier and the evidence separately

Start with the exact identifier, then compare its confidence label and notes. Name-derived means we can parse the words but have not traced the behavior. Interpreted means the context is stronger. Code-referenced means implementation evidence exists; it is still not a promise that Google has enabled the feature for your account, language or device.

A safe way to explore

Prefer ordinary Gboard settings first. On a compatible patched build, record the current flag value and Gboard version, change one parameter at a time, and reproduce the specific behavior in the same app and language. Undo changes that cause startup problems or unreliable input. Treat root-only tools as inspection instruments, not as evidence that the option is effective.

Frequently asked questions

Are these official user-facing settings?

Usually not. The Atlas includes internal identifiers and experimental configuration, not a Google-approved list of user options.

Does finding a flag mean it works?

No. Feature eligibility, server configuration and compiled code paths can all limit what happens.

Gboard Emoji Kitchen Flags, Browse UI and AI Ranking

Find the flags related to Emoji Kitchen discovery, zero-state suggestions, animation and embedding-based ranking.

What you should know

Emoji Kitchen has separate browsing, suggestion, animation and ranking systems; one toggle rarely controls the entire experience.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Separate the content from its entry points

Emoji Kitchen can involve suggested emoji combinations, a browsing panel and contextual chips. enable_emoji_kitchen_browse_entry_point_v2 suggests a revised way to enter browsing, whereas enable_emoji_kitchen_for_zero_state_emojis concerns suggestions without a typed query. A visible control does not guarantee the associated sticker assets or ranker are ready.

Why multiple model names appear

The catalog contains references to an embedding index, TensorFlow Lite emoji prediction and a Gemma embedding ranker. They are clues to different techniques used in searching or prioritizing expressive results. They should not be conflated with a full chatbot running inside the keyboard or evidence that every device downloads a large model.

Test discovery and rendering separately

Try opening Emoji Kitchen directly, then compare suggestions after typing the same short phrase. Note whether a combination appears, whether a search result ranks differently and whether an animation plays. These are independent observations; testing them individually produces much more useful bug reports than saying 'Emoji Kitchen works.'

Frequently asked questions

Does a Gemma flag mean the whole keyboard uses Gemma?

No. The identifier concerns a specific embedding/ranking function, not necessarily text generation.

Can I unlock every sticker with one flag?

Not reliably. Asset delivery and feature availability can be independent of browsing controls.

Why Gboard Flags Don't Work After You Enable Them

Diagnose missing controls, unchanged behavior, inactive model flags and unsupported language experiments in patched Gboard.

What you should know

A flag can exist in the APK yet do nothing because its consumer, model, locale or rollout condition is absent.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Check what you actually changed

Confirm the exact identifier, type and value; many flags differ by one prefix. For example, disable_load_v2_klp disables an internal V2 option when true. A title that drops 'disable' can reverse the meaning. Compare the record with the installed APK build rather than assuming screenshots from another release match yours.

Identify the missing dependency

An AI or speech flag may gate only the UI entry point while models, AICore, downloads, language eligibility and server-side feature access are evaluated elsewhere. Likewise, visual changes can depend on Android window mode, theme preferences or app-specific text fields. A toggle is not a substitute for code and data supporting the feature.

Use conventional troubleshooting before more flags

If Gboard lags, fails to appear or misbehaves, try Google's documented settings and cache troubleshooting before random flag changes. Clearing app storage resets settings and learned state, so record anything important first. Revert the experimental edit when the behavior is worse, instead of stacking ten more guesses.

Frequently asked questions

Does restarting always apply a flag?

No. It can reload local configuration, but cannot create missing server eligibility or bundled code.

Is an absent editor entry an error?

Not necessarily. Some Atlas entries were collected from APK strings, not from a live editor enumeration.

Gboard GIF and Sticker Prediction Flags Explained

Understand contextual GIF search, custom stickers, prediction timing and why an expression tab can differ across apps.

What you should know

Search-ranking controls, sticker prediction and UI tabs are separate from which GIFs a provider can return.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Search suggestions versus content

enable_contextual_gif_search_query_suggestion suggests recommending a search query based on nearby context; enable_prioritize_recent_gifs suggests reordering results by recency. Neither guarantees that a GIF appears in every conversation. Availability can depend on provider data, connectivity and regional or app restrictions.

Sticker generation and presentation

enable_custom_sticker_tab and enable_sticker_predictions_while_typing point at surfaces for custom content and typing-time suggestions. The catalog also includes settings for delays and rendering, but those are different layers from whether a sticker is supported at all. An animation or chip appearing is not equivalent to successful sending.

Compare surfaces in the same conversation

Check the expression tab, search, and typed suggestions separately. Use the same text in two chat apps and record whether the result is suggested, selected and actually inserted. If an experiment merely rearranges a UI panel, capture the before/after position rather than claiming that GIF quality improved.

Frequently asked questions

Why do GIF results change without a flag edit?

Online provider inventory, recent usage and context can change independently.

Are custom sticker flags guaranteed to be available?

No. The visible identifiers do not establish product entitlement or supported generation backends.

Gboard Grammar Checker and Proofreading: Flags vs Real Behavior

Compare grammar checker, LLM proofreading and on-device proofreading experiments with practical tests and clear confidence limits.

What you should know

Grammar highlighting, rewrite suggestions and proofread actions are different product surfaces even when they share AI models.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Not every writing correction is autocorrect

Autocorrection handles words as you type; grammar checking may evaluate clauses or an entire sentence. The Atlas lists enable_grammar_checker, enable_llm_based_grammar_checker and enable_on_device_proofread as distinct identifiers. Names imply separate experiment paths, but the current build may collapse them or leave some gated.

Why the editing app matters

A keyboard may present a suggestion chip in one editor but not in another. A web view, messaging field and long-form note can expose different capabilities. enable_grammar_checker_on_webview is especially relevant to this distinction, though the exact implementation is not verified from the identifier alone.

A useful evaluation set

Use a sentence with subject–verb disagreement, a sentence with misplaced punctuation and a correct sentence that should remain unchanged. Record whether the keyboard underlines text, offers a replacement, explains it or requires a manual action. A quality check should penalize false corrections as much as missed mistakes.

Frequently asked questions

Will enable_grammar_checker correct every error?

No. Language support, model availability and contextual thresholds can limit suggestions.

Does on-device_proofread guarantee offline use?

The identifier alone does not verify offline execution, even though it names a local-processing path.

Gboard Layout Flags: Keyboard Height, Floating Mode and Split Keys

Compare keyboard size and appearance controls with floating and split layouts without confusing preference flags with geometry models.

What you should know

First use Gboard's built-in settings; layout flags can be limited by screen size, window mode and hardware.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Standard settings versus experimental layout flags

A theme or keyboard-height setting usually affects appearance or touch targets. enable_adjust_default_keyboard_height and enable_number_row suggest layout preferences, while enable_key_border is visual. A screenshot change does not establish that the underlying tap-correction model was recalibrated; finger position and decoding remain related but separate.

Floating and split are context dependent

enable_auto_float_keyboard_in_landscape and enable_auto_float_keyboard_in_multi_window refer to automatic behavior in certain window states. enable_split_keyboard_on_tablet_large signals a tablet-specific layout condition. Trying to infer support on a small phone from a flag name alone can create misleading reports.

Keep typing tests fair

Compare one-handed and two-handed typing with the same app, device posture and locale. Record screen size, orientation, Android version and whether the UI is floating, split or docked. If the keyboard gets smaller, measure how comfortable and accurate it feels before claiming a particular rendering option makes typing faster.

Frequently asked questions

Does a split-keyboard flag work on every phone?

No. The identifier itself advertises a tablet/large-display condition.

Can smaller keys improve decoding accuracy?

A geometry change alone does not guarantee that; accuracy should be tested separately.

Gboard Multilingual Typing and Language Switching Flags

Distinguish multilingual typing, language prompts and locale-specific experiments before changing your keyboard setup.

What you should know

The language selected, model installed, and per-language eligibility often matter more than an isolated flag.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Why language state matters

Multilingual typing is not identical to adding two layouts to Gboard. The keyboard may maintain a primary locale, detect a language from context, and select separate correction and suggestion resources. enable_multilingual_typing and enable_crank_for_primary_locale_in_multilingual indicate parts of this internal policy, but their combined behavior isn't fully documented.

Japanese, Chinese and English are not interchangeable cases

Predictive models, gesture input, voice recognition and punctuation behavior can differ by script and installed language pack. A flag that appears during English QWERTY typing may be irrelevant to a Japanese 12-key or handwriting method. When reporting a result, always include the exact language layout and whether a speech or decoder pack was downloaded.

Test switching rather than guessing

Use the standard Gboard language selector first. Compare the same language-switch action in a text field before experimenting with prompt or order settings. Record whether the visible layout changes, whether autocorrection language changes, and whether a bilingual suggestion appears. An apparent English improvement can mask worse suggestions in another language.

Frequently asked questions

Will a flag download languages for me?

Not necessarily. Layout and model availability are separate from the existence of a configuration identifier.

Can I use the same results on every locale?

No. Test results should always specify language and input method.

Gboard Next-Word Prediction and Smart Suggestions Flags

A practical guide to next-word prediction, multiword suggestions, user-history signals and inline suggestion experiments.

What you should know

NWP and inline suggestions are different stages of suggesting text, and neither should be confused with autocorrection.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Prediction is not a single feature

Gboard may surface next-word predictions, multiword completions, inline suggestions or context-dependent chips. Their signals can include the typed prefix, language, earlier context and on-device history. Flags such as enable_nwp_tflite_engine refer to implementation choices, not a universal option that increases intelligence.

Look at the presentation layer too

enable_inline_suggestions_on_decoder_side and enable_inline_suggestions_on_client_side imply separate processing points. If a result appears in one text field and not another, the receiving application may matter. Treat a UI hint as different evidence from changes in model quality or speed.

Compare useful examples

Type a familiar three-word prefix, repeat it in multiple apps and record whether suggestions appear, how many words they span and whether tapping them inserts exactly the expected text. Repeat after any change using the same locale, model state and connectivity. Resist the temptation to change both a model flag and a suggestion-strip flag together.

Frequently asked questions

Why do suggestions vary between apps?

Different text-field capabilities and app integration can influence the UI, even when the same keyboard is active.

Is NWP the same as autocorrect?

No. Next-word prediction offers future text; autocorrection revises or replaces what you typed.

Gboard Offline Speech Packs, Language Models and Download Flags

Investigate speech pack downloads, metered connections and on-device model resources without assuming a flag enables offline dictation.

What you should know

Speech model downloads and UI availability are separate; a download flag alone cannot guarantee offline voice typing.

Evidence standard: these are real catalog identifiers, but their effects can be inferred, version-specific, or gated. Check the confidence and APK notes before changing settings.

Understand the pack lifecycle

The catalog exposes allow_metered_small_speech_pack_downloads and force_speech_language_pack_updates alongside other speech parameters. Names like these suggest conditions around model transfer and refresh, not that offline recognition is guaranteed for every language. A speech system may also have separate punctuation, capitalization and accent-enhancement models.

What the inspected APK adds

The GboardWu 18.5.4 APK contained resource URLs under dl.google.com/gboard/klp/experiment/smartdictation, including language-specific .tflite files and protobuf-style resources. That is concrete evidence that speech-related model assets can be distributed separately. It does not tell us whether a particular model is installed, current or activated in your account.

Test offline operation carefully

First ensure the chosen language's voice typing works normally. Then compare a short dictation sample with connectivity disabled, without confusing microphone permission failures with network requirements. Record language and device, and observe whether recognition begins, completes locally or requests another resource. Restore connectivity and baseline settings afterward.

Frequently asked questions

Does downloading a speech pack prove offline voice works?

No. Runtime eligibility and the recognition backend still matter.

Should I force language-pack updates?

Only with a concrete compatibility reason; forced downloads can consume storage and data.
